name: An Intellectual History of Political Liberalism
description: Political liberalism has established itself as the most dominant conceptual paradigm in contemporary global political discourses. Both its proponents and opponents often consider its principles to be timeless universals and pay little attention to their historical evolution. This course is an attempt to address this gap with the aim of arriving at a more historically and conceptually accurate understanding of its principles. It will trace the evolution of the political thought in the Greek city-states; the Roman empire; the feudal polities of the Middle Ages; critically review the notion of emergence of the modern as a radical break in the political thought of the Renaissance and the Reformation; political thought of the English Revolution; foundational thinkers of the Anglo-American liberal tradition like Thomas Hobbes, John Locke and John Stuart Mill; the theory of possessive individualism; the feminist critique of Lockean liberalism; and the liberal defence of colonialism.
